page: Microsoft Azure D8ds_v4 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the DDSv4 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon 8272CL processor with a base clock speed of 2.6 GHz. The configuration includes 8 dedicated vCPUs derived from 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding 4.0 GB of RAM per core. For local storage, the instance includes a bundled 307 GB local SSD and supports Premium Storage.

Performance benchmarks place the D8ds_v4 consistently in the average tier across most workloads. Its Intel Xeon processor achieves a single-core stress-ng score of 1411.18 and a multi-core score of 7424.94. Memory performance is characterized by a read-only small block cached bandwidth of 415.35 GB/sec, which drops to 50.58 GB/sec for large uncached blocks. In application-specific tests, the server handles 7.33 million Redis SET operations per second and delivers 7.25 GB/sec of static web serving throughput. However, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression is a relative weak point, scoring in the bottom 25% at 27.65 GB/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the D8ds_v4 offers a balanced resource profile, combining dedicated compute, moderate memory density, and local SSD storage without the premium cost of specialized memory-optimized or GPU-accelerated hardware. This makes it a viable option for general-purpose workloads, web serving, software compilation, and database operations that benefit from local high-speed SSD caching.
